title: Scott's tent found, 1912 — the diary in the snow, eight months later
sources: Wikipedia: Terra Nova Expedition — Scott and four companions reached the South Pole on 17 January 1912 and found that Amundsen had preceded them by 34 days; on 18 January they found Amundsen's tent; Oates walked out of the tent into a blizzard, saying "I am just going outside and may be some time"; Scott, Wilson and Bowers were halted 11 miles (18 km) south of One Ton Depot by a blizzard on 20 March; Scott's last diary entry, 29 March 1912, ends "For God's sake look after our people"; Cherry-Garrard and Dimitri waited at One Ton Depot and turned back on 10 March, when Scott's party was 55 miles south

Wikipedia: Robert Falcon Scott — the bodies were discovered by a search party on 12 November 1912; Tryggve Gran described the tent "snowcovered til up above the door, with Scott in the middle"; their final camp became their tomb, the tent roof lowered over the bodies

Wikipedia: Lawrence Oates; Apsley Cherry-Garrard — on 12 November the bodies of Scott, Wilson and Bowers were found in their tent, with their diaries, records and geological specimens; Oates's body was never found
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 2014 the Philae lander touches down on comet 67P; 1892 William Heffelfinger is paid $500 to play football, the first known professional player

Film: The Great White Silence (1924), Herbert Ponting, public domain. Photos and painting (public domain): the polar party at the pole; Amundsen's tent (Polheim); Scott in the Cape Evans hut, 1911; Oates, 1911; Terra Nova; "The Last Rest"; "A Very Gallant Gentleman" (Dollman, 1913); a grotto in an iceberg

post.facebook:
On this day in 1912, a search party in Antarctica found a tent half-buried in snow. Inside lay Captain Robert Falcon Scott, between Edward Wilson and Henry Bowers — with their diaries and the rock samples they had hauled from the mountains.

Scott's team of five had reached the South Pole on 17 January 1912, only to find a Norwegian tent already there: Roald Amundsen had beaten them by 34 days. On the march home, frostbite crippled them. Lawrence Oates walked out of the tent into a blizzard; his last words, Scott wrote, were "I am just going outside and may be some time."

A dog team had waited for them at One Ton Depot, and turned back on 10 March — when Scott's party was only 55 miles away. Then a blizzard trapped the last three, 11 miles from the depot. Scott's last entry, on 29 March, ends: "For God's sake look after our people."

The searchers lowered the tent over them and left it as their tomb.

Also on 12 November: the Philae lander touched down on a comet (2014), and William Heffelfinger became the first known paid football player (1892).

12 November 1912: a search party in Antarctica found Captain Scott's tent buried in snow, with Scott, Wilson and Bowers inside, and their diaries. They had reached the South Pole 34 days after Roald Amundsen. On the way back Lawrence Oates walked out into a blizzard ("I am just going outside and may be some time"), a dog team turned back only 55 miles away, and the last three were trapped 11 miles from food. Scott's last entry: "For God's sake look after our people."

Also on 12 November: Philae lands on a comet (2014) and the first known pro football player is paid (1892).
